title: Elect one physical block leader and test unequal grid-barrier arrivals
applies_when: A CUDA block-level arrival protocol is emitted for multidimensional thread blocks, especially a cooperative grid barrier that publishes one arrival per block.
lesson: Check all thread dimensions when electing the one physical block leader: tid.x == 0 alone also selects threads with nonzero y or z. A balanced one-dimensional control may hide duplicate arrivals. Add native multidimensional controls with a finite device-side delay before one block arrives, assert cross-block visibility, and repeat barrier reuse. When replacing an external DSL helper, isolate or disable compiled-kernel caches so the tested cubin actually includes that helper revision.
avoid_when: Warp-scoped or intentionally multi-participant protocols may require different leader rules. Correct block leader election does not establish concurrent-launch state isolation, correct memory fencing, or a performance gain. The cited native regression is scoped to CuTeDSL cooperative launch; it is not a full current-main compiler rebuild or a proof for other backends.

evidence.note: The baseline PTX elects arrivals by tid.x alone; source evidence of the multidimensional leader defect.
The native regression covers one-dimensional and y/z-dimensional blocks, delays one block using the device clock, checks visibility and repeats barrier reuse.

Reports baseline [1, 3] instead of [3, 3], followed by two fresh candidate runs passing all four thread shapes on RTX 5090 with private CuTeDSL 4.7. It discloses existing TileLang compiler use, cache isolation and absence of concurrency/performance claims.
